what_reading_production_changed.migration_167_is_dropped: The plan proposed backfilling go_live_date from window_end. Production has window_end on 2 of 11 sets, window_start on 8, content_end_date on 0, and production_mode on 1 of 6 contracts. Deriving a launch day for nine live sets from a null column would be inventing dates for real campaigns. So there is NO backfill: a set with go_live_date IS NULL is a pre-set-first set and the existing window fallback keeps serving it. Three migrations touching live rows across the programme becomes two, and neither is in this stage.

SB-30 is largely an ASSEMBLY over columns that exist. Only channels_json and formats_json are new, and both are moving DOWN from the set rather than being invented.

migration_runner_fault_found: run-164.js and its siblings read .env.prod-backup for --dry and .env for the REAL run. In this working copy .env points at LOCALHOST — so the dry run inspects production and a real run would have applied to a local database and printed COMMITTED. Which database is being written to must never be a side effect of a different flag. run-165-166.js now takes an EXPLICIT --dry or --apply, reads prod credentials for both, PRINTS THE HOST before touching anything, refuses when neither or both flags are given (exit 2), and refuses --apply against localhost. 163 and 164 were verified present in production, so they did reach it by some other path.

server_built.model: backend/src/services/setShape.model.js — SHOOT_MODES (three, what the column accepts), SHOOT_MODES_OFFERED (TWO, what the wizard offers), goLiveDayOf() with the pre-set-first fallback, validateSetShape() which never throws.

two_decisions_in_the_code: updateSet validates the MERGED shape, not just the fields sent — posting invites_close_at alone is still checked against the STORED go_live_date.
An existing go-live day is NOT re-checked against the lead time. A set built last week may launch tomorrow; re-validating would make a set uneditable simply because time passed.
server_built.duplicate_set: Carries the shape across. Without it a copied set silently loses its day and mode and reads as pre-set-first.
server_built.mutation_tested: 13 ways. Model 7: wizard offering remote; shipment needing both marks; the fallback reading window_end before go_live_date; lead time 5->4; the invites-close check inverted; a set with no day inventing today; validate throwing on rubbish. Controller 6: dropping a column from the INSERT; dropping a VALUE while keeping the column; not reading a field off req.body; calling validateSetShape and ignoring the answer; updateSet validating only what was sent; duplicate dropping the shape. server_built.the_tests_caught_themselves_first: The controller test extracts the INSERT block by scanning for its closing bracket. The first version scanned for the next ] — which lands inside JSON.stringify(assets_json) : '[]', truncating the block three lines early and hiding the exact fields the file exists to check. Four tests failed, correctly, on the HELPER rather than the controller. A source-reading test that quietly reads the wrong source is the same fault in a different coat.
